title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: There are two alternatives; either you apply to organizations personally or wait for the summer practice opportunities announced by the department. The second option is more risky and the capacity is usually very limited. Certain firms require the department to determine the candidates for summer practice. In that case, an announcement is made and the students are required to send their transcripts, resumes and fill out the Preference Form available under >Forms. If the student is assigned through the department, it is mandatory that the summer practice is conducted at that company.

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: Which departments of the organization should I visit during my summer practice? It is preferable for you to take an all-around trip in an organization. However, do not forget that you can still gather many observations through effective communications. You inquire about the overall operations in your practice organization although you are stationed at a particular department.

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: What kind of topics will I be studying during the practice term?

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: Industrial engineering has a broad application area. Its main field of interest is systems run by people for the needs of others, in general. Summer practice is your first lengthy period of observing and inquiring about systems in operation. Try as much as you can, to relate things you have covered in your courses to what you experience during your practice term. Learn about the many possible ways of getting various organizational and technical functions performed. Identify the systems behind all those activities. Use your "Summer Practice Manual" to guide you through this effort.

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: What sort of branches or divisions in a bank are suitable for an IE 400 practice organization?

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: As in many organizations banks have numerous activities in providing services to their customers. You should be more interested in the systems (for example organizational, information related, procedural, managerial) aspects in this service provision. In IE 400 Summer Practice you are required to observe and analyze a purposeful system in real life. Divisions or branches in a bank are suitable in that regard so much as they consist of integrated operation of people, financial resources, processes and information with some performance expectation, and they have ongoing decision making (for example, planning or evaluation) or development (for example, new services) as their required function.

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: Fill out the online questionnaire (will be announced) What constitutes a "sufficient" IE problem definition in IE 400 reports? This is described in Appendix A of your IE 400 Summer Practice Manual. You are required to supply your own description of the components of a problem formulation and justify your points. You should be specific to your practice organization. Problem identification should be the result of some methodical analysis carried out in the system the problem is associated with. Alternative courses of action and constraining factors should be supported by problem specific facts.

text: The critical issue is to see the analogies. If not exactly the same, you can identify areas of similar nature in a service organization. A budget allocation might substitute a production plan, preclassified records may stand as inventory, timetables for professionals can be counted as their schedules, from flow may replace material flow. Try to highlight the reasons you think justify such similarities in your case.

text: What sort of reporting is acceptable if several students practice in the same organization? Every practioner will have a separate report as a rule. General outlook at the firm can be common for IE 400 only. However, you should choose separate examples each for reporting on your observations.

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: If I am planning to work on a project full-time at the summer practice organization, is it possible for me to present the project work, instead of performing a practice according to the guidelines and submitting its results? IE 400 practice may involve a project type study in which students have to supply a project report as explained in "IE 400 Summer Practice Manual" instead of defining an IE problem. Minimum duration for this type of IE 400 practice is 30 workdays (6 weeks). The project may be initiated long before you started your summer practice, or may be offered specifically to you by the organization, or you deem it as a potential area worth studying there. You may also consider getting fully involved in an ongoing project during your practice and desire to report on that only in your report.

title: FAQ |  Industrial Engineering Summer Practice
text: These students need to submit a two-pages project proposal. The proposal should include brief description of the company and details of the proposed project and an outline of what you will include in the report. Note that proposal should be approved (signed) by the company and be submitted to the summer practice committee by the first week of the summer practice. The committee shall evaluate the validity of your proposed work as a substitute for IE 400 summer practice. If it fulfills the requirements of the summer practice with the necessary observations you are expected to make, then you can submit a specially qualified report. The committee may ask you to add some parts from the regular content of the guidelines as well. However, in any case your report should be complete, in that you should describe all the phases of the work done including the issue, the organizational environment, the data or the facts collected, all the tools used, the outcomes of the project and its implementation.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What is IE 300?
A: IE 300 is the first compulsory summer practice course for METU Industrial Engineering students. It is typically done after the second year and requires a minimum of 20 working days (4 weeks) at an approved company. The student must prepare a summer practice report following the IE 300 manual guidelines.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What is IE 400?
A: IE 400 is the second compulsory summer practice course for METU Industrial Engineering students. It is typically done after the third year and requires a minimum of 20 working days (4 weeks). For project-based internships, it must be at least 6 weeks. The student must prepare a report following the IE 400 manual (manufacturing or service sector version).

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What are the prerequisites for IE 300?
A: To be eligible for IE 300, students must have completed at least two years of the IE undergraduate program and be registered for the IE 300 course. The internship must be done at a company approved by the IE Summer Practice Committee.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What are the prerequisites for IE 400?
A: To be eligible for IE 400, students must have completed IE 300 successfully and be registered for the IE 400 course. The internship must be done at a different company than IE 300 unless approved by the SP Committee.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: How many working days is the summer practice?
A: Both IE 300 and IE 400 require a minimum of 20 working days (4 weeks). For IE 400 project-based internships, the minimum duration is 6 weeks (30 working days). Weekends and public holidays do not count as working days.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What documents do I need for summer practice?
A: Required documents include: the SP application form (IE300 or IE400 version), the internship work contract (staj sözleşmesi) signed by the company and the university, SGK insurance application through the OCW system, health declaration forms (beyanname), and the unemployment fund contribution form. After completing the internship, you must submit your summer practice report.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: How do I apply for SGK insurance for my internship?
A: SGK (Social Security Institution) insurance for interns is mandatory in Turkey. You must apply through the OCW system provided by METU before starting your internship. Read the instructions in the General Information section of sp-ie.metu.edu.tr carefully before applying. The university covers the SGK insurance cost for eligible students.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Can I do my internship remotely or online?
A: No. Summer internships must be done by physically attending the workplace. Remote or online internships are not accepted for IE 300 or IE 400.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What is a project-based internship for IE 400?
A: A project-based internship for IE 400 allows students to work on a specific engineering project instead of a traditional internship. It must be at least 6 weeks long. Before starting, you must submit a detailed proposal to the SP Committee describing the internship content. The internship can only begin after the proposal is approved.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Can I do my internship abroad through Erasmus?
A: Yes. Within the Erasmus program, it is possible to do an internship through Student Internship Mobility. Internships are generally in Europe for a minimum of 3 months and a maximum of 12 months. A 3-month Erasmus internship can only be counted as one of IE 300 or IE 400, not both. For more details, check the METU Erasmus office website.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Can I do my internship at a public institution?
A: Yes, but all public institutions in Turkey (kamu kurumları) accept internship applications through a centralized system. You must apply through that system. Please consult the relevant page on sp-ie.metu.edu.tr for further information.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What is the difference between IE 400 manufacturing and service manuals?
A: IE 400 has two different report manuals depending on the type of company. The manufacturing manual is for students doing their internship at manufacturing/production companies. The service manual is for students at service-sector companies (e.g., logistics, consulting, finance). You must use the correct manual based on your internship company type.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: How do I get my internship contract signed?
A: If you need your SP work contract (staj sözleşmesi) to be signed by the university, leave it at the Undergraduate Secretary Office (IE 129) and pick it up in one week.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Where do I submit my summer practice report?
A: Summer practice reports are submitted according to the deadlines announced on sp-ie.metu.edu.tr. Reports must follow the format described in the IE 300 or IE 400 manual. Submission details and deadlines are announced on the official SP website and through the department.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What happens if my internship is rejected?
A: If your summer practice application or report is rejected by the SP Committee, you will need to redo the internship or revise your report based on the feedback given. Make sure to follow the manual guidelines carefully and have your application approved before starting the internship.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: When is the summer practice period?
A: Summer practices are typically done during the summer semester (July–August). The exact dates and deadlines for applications and report submissions are announced each year on the official METU-IE Summer Practice website at sp-ie.metu.edu.tr/en.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Do I need to find the company myself?
A: Yes, students are generally responsible for finding their own internship company. The company must be approved by the IE SP Committee. You can check the SP website for lists of previously approved companies or guidance on finding suitable companies.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What sections must the IE 300 report include?
A: The IE 300 summer practice report must follow the structure defined in the IE 300 manual. It includes sections covering the company background, production/service processes, quality management, safety, and IE-related observations. The report must address specific questions listed in each section of the manual.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What sections must the IE 400 report include?
A: The IE 400 report structure depends on whether you use the manufacturing or service manual. Both manuals include sections on company overview, operations management, industrial engineering applications, and a personal evaluation section. Refer to the appropriate manual for detailed section requirements.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Who evaluates the summer practice report?
A: Summer practice reports are evaluated by the METU Industrial Engineering Summer Practice Committee. The committee reviews whether the report meets the format and content requirements specified in the relevant manual (IE 300 or IE 400). Company supervisors also fill in the evaluation form for the student.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What is the evaluation form?
A: The evaluation form (evaluation_form_english) is filled by the company supervisor at the end of the internship. It assesses the student's performance, behavior, and contribution during the internship. The sealed evaluation form is sent directly to the IE department by the company.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Can I contact the department if I have more questions?
A: Yes, but the department asks students to first check the SP website (sp-ie.metu.edu.tr/en) and the meeting slides carefully before sending an email. If your question is not answered there, you may contact the SP Committee by email. The undergraduate secretary office (IE 129) can also assist with document-related matters.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: What is the SP application form?
A: The SP application form is the official form you submit to the IE department before starting your internship. There are separate forms for IE 300 and IE 400 (sp_application_form_ie300_eng and sp_application_form_ie400_eng). The form includes details about the company, internship dates, and must be approved before you begin.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Can IE 300 and IE 400 be done at the same company?
A: Generally, IE 300 and IE 400 must be done at different companies. However, exceptions may be granted by the SP Committee in special cases. You must get approval from the committee before proceeding.

title: FAQ – METU-IE Summer Practice
text:
Q: Is the summer practice graded as pass/fail?
A: Yes, the summer practice courses (IE 300 and IE 400) are evaluated on a pass/fail basis. If your report and internship meet the requirements of the manual and the SP Committee's standards, you receive a passing grade.
